newsitem.title: CANADA: Chretien sees 1996/97 deficit at C$16 bln or less.
newsitem.headline: Chretien sees 1996/97 deficit at C$16 bln or less.

text.p: Canadian Prime Minister Jean Chretien said on Tuesday the budget deficit for fiscal 1996/97 ended March 31 should come in at C$16 billion or lower.
"Rather than C$42 billion (when the Liberal government took office) it will be around C$16, C$15 or C$14 (billion) he said in a television interview.
"It looks as if it's going to be C$16 billion."
"We had to put the finances of the nation in order. It's done," Chretien said.
However, he also said when asked about the possibility of tax breaks for small businesses, "We have to stay the course. We have to finish to reduce. Otherwise we will go back to where we were."

During his current election campaign tour in Vancouver, he said his government would defend medicare, old age pensions and social programs but he also said, "Today we're talking about the timing of the next tax cuts."
In a speech on Tuesday morning he said that Canada was in the best position economically it had seen in years.
"We are on the verge of tremendous economic growth."
Canada will hold a federal election on June 2.
